title: Question
description: An unresolved question, tracked as an object rather than a sentence in a document (REQ-0014). Stage 4's question backlog. ⚠️ It owns state nothing else can hold: whether it has been answered, what the answer was, and what is waiting on it — none of which is derivable from any other artifact. That is why it passes #41 where the remaining two activated types still have to argue for themselves (#106).

allOf.$comment: An answered question must say what the answer is, or point at what settled it. Nested inside allOf per #82.

then.$comment: A question marked answered with neither an answer nor a link to what settled it is the backlog's version of a well-formed false success — it looks closed and records nothing.

statement.description: The question, stated so that an answer would be recognisable as one. Same field name as every other type's payload (#82).

resolution.description: ⚠️ A THIRD axis, distinct from reviewStatus and lifecycle (#82), because it answers a third question. reviewStatus is where the artifact sits in review; lifecycle is whether it still stands; this is whether the QUESTION has been settled. A question can be approved, active and entirely unanswered — collapsing any two of these would lose exactly that state.

answer.description: What the answer turned out to be. Prose is right here: an answer that anything downstream must traverse should be an assertion or a decision, and this field is what remains when nothing does (#41).

answeredBy.description: What settled it — a decision taken, evidence gathered, or an assertion that now carries the claim.

blocks.description: What is waiting on this question. Stage 4's exit criterion is that every BLOCKING gap has a decision recorded, so which gaps block is state the gate needs and nothing else holds.

tags.description: Changing tags never invalidates an approval (#103).

x-ownsIrreducibleState.description: #41's test, applied explicitly before building rather than assumed from activation (#106). A question is traversed — decision.addresses, assertion.openQuestions, requirement.openQuestions all point at it — and it holds `resolution`, `answer` and `blocks`, none of which any other artifact can supply. An unanswered question is not the absence of a decision; it is a tracked thing with a state.

x-unresolvableTraceTargets.description: #75: research-finding, runbook-step, schema and api-spec are not all implemented or activated here.
